correctness.rationale: For every smooth quartic del Pezzo, the sixteen lines have a triangle-free Clebsch intersection graph. Each fixed exceptional curve contributes q+1 rational points, double fixed intersections subtract once, and Frobenius-swapped intersecting pairs each add exactly one rational point, giving f(q+1)-a+b on the union. Weil–Lefschetz gives ambient count q²+(1+t)q+1. Exact standard-library enumeration of all 1920 even signed permutations produces the 18 complete classes, root traces and correction counts; the table and zero classifications were replayed. Concrete F3 and F5 blowup models realize both zero regimes; F7 is independently enumerated. No finite experiment is used in place of the universal geometric proof.

value.rationale: The exact arithmetic count of rational points off all exceptional curves is a natural geometric question in finite-field del Pezzo rational-point and unirationality constructions. The result answers it uniformly for all Frobenius actions, isolates rational points from conjugate exceptional-line intersections, and sharply classifies the only two possible zero regimes, with explicit realized examples and a uniform nonempty result above five field elements. This complete stratification is more useful than a split-surface special case.
